order: Stop answering the question of whether scratch sits inside the repository by comparing path strings. Short names on Windows, private var paths on macOS, and differing separators and case each make a directory plainly inside the repository compare as outside, voiding the guarantee that a review must never write into the tree it is reviewing. Ask git instead, running rev-parse show-toplevel from both the project and the candidate and comparing git's two answers. Keep string comparison only as the backstop for a candidate git cannot see. Route every place that asks the question through the new check, both the pre-creation validation of a configured scratch root and the post-creation check on the runner's own directory, answering a candidate that does not exist yet from its deepest existing ancestor. Make the orphan sweep count a directory when it was deregistered or removed, and have the isolation negative control report itself inconclusive by name where it does not reproduce.
claims: Rev-parse show-toplevel runs from the project and the candidate, and git's answers are compared. Both call sites were converted, the pre-creation validation of a configured scratch root and the post-creation check on the runner's directory; a grep of the runner finds the string helper referenced exactly once, as its fallback, and a hand run on a short-name path had both gates refuse. The sweep counts a directory it deregistered or removed, and the isolation control names itself inconclusive where it cannot reproduce.
